value.content:
In SQLite, an orders screen looks up one customer's orders in a 1 million row table. Without an index, the plan is SCAN: the database reads the whole table. With CREATE INDEX on the customer column, the plan becomes SEARCH: the lookup walks down the index tree to the rows. The price: every new order also goes into the index.

Measured on this machine: SQLite 3.46.1, Python 3.14, Ryzen 7 5700U, 15 runs with the database rebuilt, SQLite default cache. Medians: query without index 85.7 ms; with index 0.047 ms; writing 10 thousand orders 24.3 ms without the index and 318.9 ms with it; building the index 736 ms; file from 74.6 to 87.2 MB.

Mechanism source: SQLite documentation (Query Planning, EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and file format).

The voice is mine, cloned with AI. The animations were made for this video.
